title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Large Language Models to a Low-Resource Agglutinative Language: A Corpus, Datasets, and a Reproducible Benchmark for the Bashkir Language
abstract: arXiv:2610.31397v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Bashkir is a low-resource agglutinative language written in Cyrillic and remains poorly represented in modern LLMs. We present an open resource suite and a systematic benchmark of adaptation methods: the Bashkir Web Corpus (71,567 documents, 46.9M tokens, 16 sources) and three labelled datasets for binary, multiclass and multilabel text classification; the benchmark covers the first two. Experiments use eight architectures (82M-8B: DistilGPT2, GPT-2 base/medium, Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B, YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B, mBERT, XLM-R) and three adaptation groups (full fine-tuning, QLoRA, in-context learning), plus continual pretraining (CPT). (1) QLoRA on 3.8-8B models outperforms encoder-only fine-tuning on binary classification: YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B with CPT reaches macro-F1 0.748 vs 0.653 (XLM-R) and 0.650 (mBERT); pairwise differences are significant after Holm correction (p<0.001). (2) YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B significantly outperforms Mistral-7B and Ph

translated_title: 大语言模型向低资源黏着语的参数高效适配：面向巴什基尔语的语料库、数据集与可复现基准
translated_abstract: 巴什基尔语是一种使用西里尔字母书写的低资源黏着语，在现代大语言模型中的代表性仍然不足。我们提出了一套开放资源套件和适配方法的系统性基准测试：巴什基尔语网络语料库（71,567篇文档、4690万词元、16个来源），以及三个分别用于二分类、多分类和多标签文本分类的标注数据集；该基准测试涵盖前两种分类任务。实验使用了八种架构（参数规模82M-8B：DistilGPT2、GPT-2 base/medium、Phi-3-mini、Mistral-7B、YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B、mBERT、XLM-R）和三种适配方法（全量微调、QLoRA、上下文学习），并辅以持续预训练（CPT）。实验结果表明：（1）在二分类任务上，对3.8-8B参数模型应用QLoRA优于仅编码器模型的微调：结合CPT的YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B达到宏平均F1值0.748，而XLM-R为0.653、mBERT为0.650；经Holm校正后两两差异均显著（p<0.001）。（2）YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B显著优于Mistral-7B和Ph……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文发布了巴什基尔语的开放语料库、标注数据集及系统性适配基准，证明基于QLoRA的参数高效适配结合持续预训练，可使3.8-8B参数的大语言模型在该低资源黏着语的文本分类任务上显著超越传统编码器模型微调。
en_tdlr: This paper releases an open corpus, labeled datasets, and a systematic adaptation benchmark for Bashkir, showing that parameter-efficient QLoRA adaptation with continual pretraining enables 3.8-8B LLMs to significantly outperform fine-tuned encoder models on text classification for this low-resource agglutinative language.
